::: {.hero} ::: {.hero-text} ::: {.name} Kamil Gacek, MBA ::: ::: {.role} PhD Student in Economics and Finance
Research and Teaching Assistant ::: ::: {.affil} Department of Applications of Mathematics in Economics
Faculty of Management, [AGH University of Krakow](https://www.agh.edu.pl/en)
Krakow, Poland ::: ::: ![](images/profile.jpg){.portrait fig-alt="Portrait of Kamil Gacek"} ::: ::: {.tags} - Input–Output Analysis - Environmentally Extended IO - Water Footprint - Structural Decomposition Analysis - Structural Path Analysis - Dynamic Inoperability IO Models - Drought and Disaster Risk - Environmental Economics - Applied Mathematics ::: ## Research I am a Research and Teaching Assistant at the Faculty of Management, AGH University of Krakow. My research combines environmental economics with applied mathematical modelling, and it starts from a question that is harder than it looks: ::: {.pullquote} What does a water shortage actually cost an economy that does not think of itself as water-dependent? ::: Most of the water an industry relies on it never touches. It arrives embedded in inputs — in materials, energy, food, transport — which means that a drought hits sectors that have no visible connection to it, and hits them late enough that the link is easy to miss. I use Input–Output frameworks to make that structure visible, to attribute a rising water footprint to the forces behind it, and to translate a shortage into the losses that accumulate along each sector's recovery path. The point is to move the question from after to before: to let a shortage be simulated rather than surveyed, and mitigation strategies compared before they are needed. You can read more about my research [here](research.qmd). Alongside this I have been a research assistant in the POLPAN project at the Institute of Philosophy and Sociology of the Polish Academy of Sciences since 2024, working on statistical analysis of the 1988–2023 longitudinal panel. I also sit on the Discipline Council for Economics and Finance at AGH. ## Education I studied at the Jagiellonian University in Krakow, where I completed a Bachelor's in Mathematics (2020), a Master's in Applied Mathematics (2022) and a second Bachelor's, in Finance, Banking and Insurance (2022). In 2025 I completed an MBA at WSB University in Krakow. Since 2023 I have been a doctoral candidate in Economics and Finance at AGH University of Krakow, writing a dissertation on Input–Output models in disaster impact assessment under the supervision of Prof. Łukasz Lach and Dr Anna Dubel. In 2025 I took part in TopMinds, a mentoring programme run by the Polish–American Fulbright Commission and Top 500 Innovators. ## Industry For the past five years I have worked in people analytics in global engineering organisations — currently as HR Data Analyst Partner at Jacobs, and before that at Aptiv, where I moved from an internship to a lead analyst role. In both cases the work sits in a global team supporting the whole organisation on HR analytics: ad hoc questions, individual reports and studies, modelling and day-to-day support for the business, alongside long-running analytical projects that I take through every stage, from the business context and the requirements to building, testing and maintaining what comes out of them. You can read more about my industry work [here](industry.qmd). ## Elsewhere ::: {.linklist} - [[]{.bi .bi-linkedin .profile-icon}[LinkedIn]{.linklist-label}](https://www.linkedin.com/in/kamil-gacek/) - [[]{.ai .ai-google-scholar .profile-icon}[Google Scholar]{.linklist-label}](https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=Bo11EggAAAAJ&hl=pl) - [[]{.ai .ai-researchgate .profile-icon}[Research Gate]{.linklist-label}](https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Kamil-Gacek-2) - [[]{.ai .ai-orcid .profile-icon}[ORCID]{.linklist-label}](https://orcid.org/0009-0002-0235-3232) - [[]{.ai .ai-cv .profile-icon}[Curriculum vitae]{.linklist-label}](files/CV_Kamil_Gacek.pdf) :::
